text:
maria: Heads up — our Savings Plan coverage for eu-west-1 P4/P5 during Nov dropped from 88% to 52% over the last 2 weeks.

josh: saw that in the dashboard this morning. any spike in on-demand or new instance families?

maria: looks like we shifted a chunk of inference pods to g5/ga11 after the runtime update. Tagging also got inconsistent — some workloads lost 'env:prod' tag when we patched the deployer.

trent: ok that explains instance family mismatch. Savings Plans are family/sku-sensitive so family swap kills coverage. Can we map which deployments moved and whether they can be pinned back?

maria: short list: model-batcher, spike-router, and offload-worker. batcher moved ~120 GPU hours/day to g5 last Thurs.

harper: quick mitigation: pause new g5 capacity and redeploy batcher to g4dn where SP covers. But that's risky for latency.

josh: alternatives: 1) exchange some reserved capacity via AWS console (modify RI) 2) ask acct team for one-time family exchange 3) buy short-term Convertible RI for g5.

maria: AWS rep said convertible exchanges could take 48-72h and might not fully match. We should estimate cost delta before buying.

trent: can someone run coverage delta by tag and family? I ran a quick CE query but need finer granularity.

josh: i'll run script now ->

josh: ```
aws ce get-savingsplans-utilization-detail --time-period Start=2025-11-01,End=2025-11-14 --filter file://filters.json
```

harper: also check orphaned usage: spot launch templates missing 'billing-project' tag. Those show as on-demand in some reports.

maria: action items: A) josh produce per-deployment family-hour report by EOD B) harper run tag remediation job C) trent draft cost-delta calc for temporary RI purchases D) harper/open ticket with AWS for exchange

trent: for calc, assume 60% of the 36k GPU-hours moved can be recovered by switching back; if not, buying 1-month of g5 convertible may be cheaper than paying on-demand.

aws-billing-bot: Notice: Reserved Instance utilization dropped 36% in eu-west-1 (period 2025-11-01 to 2025-11-14). See bill.redwood.internal/ri/coverage

josh: uploaded raw csv to /shared/infra/savings/coverage-whiplash-1728609999.csv

maria: thanks. let's meet 09:00 UTC tomorrow to decide buy vs roll-back. If we roll back, coordinate with runtime to avoid latency regression. :calendar:

harper: will also add a guard to deployer to preserve billing tags on patching.

maria: cool. tagging this thread 'urgent-cost' and 'coverage-investigation'.

trent: one more note — check cross-region failover policies, some scheduled tasks spun up in eu-central while eu-west was auto-scaling; that also nudged usage mix.

josh: noted. will include region split in the report.

maria: closing loop here after tomorrow's call. thx all :thumbsup:
